title: The Daniell cell
caption: Zinc (E° −0.76 V) is more easily oxidised than copper (+0.34 V), so zinc is the negative electrode (anode) and copper the positive (cathode). Electrons flow through the wire from zinc to copper; the salt bridge completes the circuit. E°cell = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.
alt: Two beakers: a zinc electrode in zinc sulfate and a copper electrode in copper sulfate, joined by a wire through a voltmeter reading 1.10 V and by a salt bridge.
description: Left: zinc in Zn²⁺(aq), the anode: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻.
Right: copper in Cu²⁺(aq), the cathode: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu.
Electrons flow along the wire from zinc to copper; the voltmeter reads 1.10 V.
A salt bridge of KNO₃(aq) joins the solutions.
